articles.title: GTA 6 Players Report Crashes on PS5 With Error CE-108255-1
articles.summary: GTA 6 players on PlayStation 5 have reported frequent crashes tied to error code CE-108255-1, and it looks like it's blocking them from progressing through the story while they wait for Sony and Rockstar to send out a fix.
articles.body:
GTA 6 players on PlayStation 5 have reported frequent crashes tied to error code CE-108255-1, and it looks like it's blocking them from progressing through the story while they wait for Sony and Rockstar to send out a fix.

Although Rockstar Games spent a decade making its new Grand Theft Auto game, it's no surprise to see the new highest-rated game of all time launching with at least a few hiccups. Some have it worse than others, though, with more than a few reports of crashes affecting PS5 consoles popping up online in the days following GTA 6's launch.

The most common cause seems to be tied to error code CE-108255-1, which, as defined by Sony , simply indicates that "an error occurred with the game/application." It seems that, although the majority of players aren't encountering the issue, those who have haven't been able to find a proper fix. Adding to the trouble is that those who have met these dreaded GTA 6 crashes are getting them pretty frequently, and what's triggering them isn't always clear. There are reports from players on both standard PS5 and PS5 Pro consoles running into these issues, with some even saying that crashes appear to be tied to the story, barring them from making any progress.

"I've noticed that the issue manifests differently for different players," one Reddit user said . "In my case, the game crashes on Jason's loading screen: it freezes and then displays the CE-108255-1 error code, meaning I can't even get into the game. Others manage to play for a few minutes before experiencing a crash. I really hope Sony and Rockstar work together to investigate and resolve this issue as soon as possible."

Game crashes are annoying for anyone, but when a massive game like GTA 6, which many feel has a less-than-generous autosave system , suddenly boots players back to the PS5 home screen without warning, it can be especially troublesome. Many who have reported the crashes to PlayStation Support say they've been directed to Rockstar, while those who report to Rockstar say they're being directed to PlayStation. One player said they feel like they're "stuck in an endless support loop, with a game I paid for and still can't play."

Meanwhile, those who have managed to get help say most assistance hasn't been able to completely resolve their issues. However, some have said they've had luck with a few tried-and-true methods, such as uninstalling and reinstalling the game, making sure both the PS5 and game have their most recent updates, and restoring licenses.

"I’ve done everything possible to solve this," another player said . "Deleted cache. Rebuilt database, deleted everything else from my console, took it apart, cleaned it, turned HDR off, switched to 1080p, went and updated game license, deleted and reinstalled and still crashing. Ugh. I’ve got a day 1 PS5 with a disc drive. Other friends of mine with the same console are playing with no issue."

Again, it's unclear if the crashing issue is tied specifically to the PS5 or GTA 6 itself. Until either entity comes up with an update, though, all affected players are stuck on launch weekend.

GTA 6 released for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S November 19 and, in its first 24 hours, made Rockstar $3.79 billion. It's the most successful launch in the history of entertainment , and although its exact unit sales have yet to be disclosed, parent company Take-Two Interactive was at least willing to share that it sold 32.5 million copies in pre-orders alone.

Just getting started in GTA 6 or wondering what to do next? Check out the Official Grand Theft Auto 6 guide right here on IGN. If you're still getting your bearings, discover GTA's new systems with the Beginner's Guide - 67 Tips and Tricks , or get all the details on the first chapters with the Chapter 1 Guide and Tips and Chapter 2 Guide and Tips . If you're already driving all around Leonida and want to know everything there is to find and do, see the Leonida interactive map .

Michael Cripe is a freelance writer with IGN. He's best known for his work at sites like The Pitch, The Escapist, and OnlySP. Be sure to give him a follow on Bluesky (@mikecripe.bsky.social) and Twitter (@MikeCripe).

articles.title: The Ecovacs Deebot T90 Pro Omni Robot Vacuum Delivers Incredible 30,000Pa Suction and More High-End Features for $549 During Black Friday
articles.summary: Give the gift of clean floors with this innovative robot vacuum.
articles.body:
Who wouldn’t love to have a few chores taken off their hands? This holiday season, give someone you love one of the most useful gifts: a brand-new robot vacuum that will leave floors sparkling. The Ecovacs Deebot T90 Pro Onmi delivers a state-of-the-art clean with boosted vacuum suction power, continuously self-washing mops, and an incredible multipurpose base station. It’s a robot vacuum with flagship features that is just $549 for Black Friday, $250 off the list price.

Score $250 Off the Ecovacs Deebot T90 Pro Onmi Robot Vacuum

ECOVACS DEEBOT T90 PRO OMNI Robot Vacuum and Mop

I test a lot of robot vacuums and have used an Ecovacs robot vacuum in my home for years. I absolutely love their reliability, innovative designs, and competitive prices. Even if I haven’t had a chance to try the Deebot T90 Pro Omni just yet, it’s sure to deliver an incredible clean, and honestly, all those high-end features under $600 are pretty unheard of.

One of my biggest issues with robot vacuums is their lack of power to pick up larger, heavier messes, especially on deep-pile carpets and rugs. The 30,000Pa boosted suction power is the highest I’ve seen and will remove more debris than your typical robot vacuum. Noise-reducing tech is built in to help keep things quieter. The roller also extends 0.6 inches beyond the body, letting it reach edges, baseboards, and more.

Mopping shouldn’t disappoint either, thanks in large part to the Ozmo 3.0 roller system. The mop self-cleans while scrubbing floors with continuous pressure rather than just wiping like typical mopping pads. The roller also lifts on carpets and rugs, so you won’t need to deal with nasty wet edges. AI tech even helps the robot vacuum precisely weave around obstacles, including pets, while cleaning.

During and after, the Deebot T90 Pro Omni returns to the base station. When docked, it automatically empties the dust box, power-washes the roller mop with hot water, and dries it. Even the robot vacuum’s dirty water system is flushed out to prevent sludge and other gunk from degrading performance over time. Plus, you can get a 10% charge in just 3 minutes for a longer cleaning time, making it a solid option for larger homes.

Danielle is a Tech freelance writer based in Los Angeles who spends her free time creating videos and geeking out over music history.

articles.title: The Binding of Isaac Dev Removes Undisclosed AI-Generated Music From Repentance+ Following Creator Response, Review-Bombing
articles.summary: The Binding of Isaac developer Nicalis has removed undisclosed AI-generated music included in Repentance+ after backlash led to a review-bombing campaign on Steam and a response from the game's creator, Edmund McMillen.
articles.body:
The Binding of Isaac developer Nicalis has removed undisclosed AI-generated music included in Repentance+ after backlash led to a review-bombing campaign on Steam and a response from the game's creator, Edmund McMillen.

McMillen and Nicalis spent months building up to the November 19, 2026, release date for the latest update in their classic action roguelike game, but that launch was quickly soured. Just 8% of The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+'s recent Steam reviews are positive, with a good chunk of comments left by players referencing AI-generated material that was not previously mentioned in any official capacity.

"Thanks, Nicalis, for breaking everything and adding AI slop to an already-existing game!" one popular review said .

Screens - The Binding of Isaac Repentance

"I'm starting to think that adding AI to a game should be valid grounds to refunds to people who have already paid for and played a game," another said . "Shameful they would do this to an Indie gem. Shameful."

The allegedly AI-generated content in question seems to be music exclusively tied to a specific, Grand Theft Auto-themed run meant to coincide with the recent release of GTA 6 . What could have been a cute jab at another gaming titan boiled into a full-blown controversy for Nicalis when Reddit user ShweetsStuff reported the questionable tunes just one day after launch.

As artificial intelligence advances, it's become increasingly difficult to discern human-made art from content pushed out by machines, but ShweetsStuff was able to provide evidence backing their claims. Specifically, they pointed to a handful of tracks that mention AI music software Suno in their metadata, which also included links to their Suno pages.

AI-generated content passed off as art has already become controversial on its own in recent years. Adding to the fire for The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+ was the fact that the music was featured in the new update without any sort of update to its Steam description. Valve requires developers to disclose how they may have used AI during game development, making the music's inclusion as puzzling as it is concerning for those who felt Nicalis had pulled the wool over their eyes.

Negative reviews poured in following ShweetsStuff's discovery, leading McMillen to issue a statement today. He said he “had no idea" how AI-generated music found its way into the launch build of The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+'s new update.

"Woke up to a s**t show," he said , "obviously I had no idea it featured generated music in the daily run, looking into how that happened and getting it removed, stay tuned."

Please report issues and bugs to the email attached. — 🜏 Edmund McMillen 🜏 (@edmundmcmillen) November 21, 2026

Please report issues and bugs to the email attached.

Just hours later, Nicalis launched a new patch, confirming the "removal of generated music files." The update is currently live for PC, with the studio adding that it has already been submitted to Microsoft, Nintendo, and Sony. When exactly it will go live for those platforms remains to be seen.

No explanation for how or why the AI-generated music was included was provided. Instead, the team simply said it was "working on the game and will continue to address new and old bugs." McMillen also encouraged fans to report issues and bugs to the developers.

In the meantime, The Binding of Isaac: Repentance+'s recent reviews on Steam remain firmly in the "Overwhelmingly Negative" category. The major update also coincided with the launch of Repentance+ on new platforms, including Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S. For more, you can read IGN's 9/10 review for The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth and our 9/10 review for Afterbirth+ .

articles.title: Watch: Should Messi have been red carded for this play vs Crew?
articles.summary: Fair to say that the Crew frustrated Leo Messi in Game 1 of their playoff matchup. Watch the Miami star throw the ball at Columbus' Gonzalo Tapia.
articles.body:
The Columbus Crew won Game 1 of their best-of-three playoff series against Inter Miami FC 3-0. Gonzalo Tapia scored twice and Patrick Schulte made five saves as Miami played most of the game down a man. The Herons were shorthanded after Gonzalo Lujan received a second yellow in the 36th minute.

Star forward Leo Messi controversially avoided a red card on this play. Instead, both he and Tapia received yellows.

Taha Habroune also scored for the Crew, who have won seven in a row in MLS play.

The No. 7 seed Crew will host the defending MLS Cup champion and No. 2 seed Miami in Game 2 on Nov. 27.

articles.title: The Cosmere RPG Core Rulebook for The Stormlight Archive Is 50% Off Today
articles.body:
Brandon Sanderson's Cosmere book universe has been expanding to the tabletop for years now. Ever since the prolific fantasy author partnered with Brotherwise Games, there's been a growing wealth of Cosmere board game adaptations worthy of your time. And right now, Amazon has dropped the price of one of the best options by 50% for Black Friday.

The Cosmere RPG isn't for casual tabletop gamers, it's more akin to a Dungeons and Dragons experience . If you enjoy the Stormlight Archive series and immersive tabletop RPGs, you're going to love diving into the world. We liked it enough to give it a solid 8 out of 10 in our review back when Stormlight version came out.

Stormlight Handbook, Cosmere RPG Core Rulebook

Amazon's Black Friday sale isn't the only reason the Stormlight Handbook is getting such a big discount. It's been a full year since it came out, and the official Mistborn expansion has just launched this month. The price drop makes it a great time to jump into the Stormlight story to see if you actually like it. At $29.99, this is the lowest price we've seen on the core rulebook since it first released.

If you want to skip the Stormlight Archive RPG, you can jump right to Mistborn instead. The handbook is the main thing you'll need if you want to build characters in either era of Mistborn. You'll also get some general guidance for GMs building out a campaign in the world of Scadriel. Since it is a Mistborn game, there's also a focus on the metallic arts of allomancy and ferochemy you wouldn't get from the Stormlight characters.

Jacob Kienlen is a Senior Audience Development Strategist and Writer for IGN. Born and raised in Portland, Oregon, he has considered the Northwest his home for his entire life. With a bachelor's degree in communication and 10 years of professional writing experience, his expertise is spread across a variety of different pop culture topics — from TV series to books and the latest LEGO sets .

articles.title: Nintendo's 2026 Black Friday Sale is Officially Live
articles.summary: Nintendo's official Black Friday sale is now live and includes a rare Switch 2 bundle discount, up to 50% off Switch 2 games, MicroSD Express cards, and more. Here's where to find all the top discounts to ensure you're saving as much as you can.
articles.body:
Nintendo's official Black Friday 2026 sale is now live across all major retailers . From Nov. 22-29, fans can score up to 50% off a slew of Switch 2 games, some top discounts on memory cards, and the first-ever official Switch 2 Black Friday deal .

That's right, we're actually getting a decent console deal during the Black Friday sales (since both PlayStation and Xbox have gone absent in this regard).

Nintendo Switch 2 + Mario Kart World Bundle

Originally priced at $549.99, including Mario Kart World and a three-month membership to Nintendo Switch Online, this Switch 2 bundle would usually save buyers around $38. But now, with the Black Friday discount applied, savings are closer to $88 in total .

That's not all, however, as there are also a slew of incredible Switch 2 games discounted in the sale. I'll include my absolute top picks just below.

Notably, the third party deals are considerably better than the Switch 2 first party games. Donkey Kong Bananza and Kirby Air Riders are standouts from Nintendo's lineup of games, but falls a little short for recent titles that fans might have been looking out for, like The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, Nintendo Switch Sports Resort, Star Fox, and more.

Nevertheless, there's still plenty of great third-party game deals to consider . That includes Resident Evil Requiem for $39.99, and Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition, for $59.99. That's just the tip of the iceberg, however, as there's so many good offers that it's hard to just list off everything on sale.

It's especially good as most of these games have been released (or re-released on Switch 2) in 2026. So, it's all new games you're getting a pretty reasonable discount on.

Super Mario Party Jamboree + Jamboree TV

Super Mario Galaxy + Super Mario Galaxy 2

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Switch 2 Digital)

Kirby and the Forgotten Land – Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Star-Crossed World (Switch 2 Digital)

Xenoblade Chronicles: Definitive Edition (Switch 2 Digital)

Donkey Kong Country Returns HD (Switch Digital)

Xenoblade Chronicles: Definitive Edition (Switch Digital)

Nintendo Kirby and the Forgotten Land (Switch Digital)

On the digital side of things , you can save a little on very recent releases, including the phenomenal The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake .

It’s only $5 off, but it just came out. Honestly, it’s the best-looking game Nintendo has ever released, and the 1998-era puzzle design holds up impossibly well . I loved every second of that game, and I look forward to replaying it in a year or so.

Samsung Nintendo Switch Memory Cards on Sale for Black Friday

One of the most welcome deals for new Switch 2 owners is on memory ! The Switch 2 only comes with 256GB of onboard storage and it will run out faster than you think. If you have a standard MicroSD card from your previous Switch, it won't work on the Switch 2.

Although the two might look similar, the MicroSD Express card is much faster than its predecessor. The Samsung P9 model boasts transfer speeds of up to 800MB/s.

So, it's good that we've found some fresh offers on Switch 2 memory cards in the Black Friday sale.

Amazon has dropped the price of the highly rated Samsung P9 256GB Micro SDXC Express Card to $44.99 with free shipping. This is a slight $3 price drop from earlier this month and the lowest price I've seen in a while.

The 512GB model is also on sale for $99.99. Are these the lowest prices ever ? No. Are there cheaper memory cards out there? Yes . But if you're looking for a memory card that we've personally tested and recommend , you won't find a better deal right now.

Quite a few games have now been released for the Switch 2 and some of them require an enormous amount of space. Final Fantasy 14 is the most gigabyte-hungry game to date, requiring about 117GB all by itself. That game alone takes up half of the Switch 2's internal storage capacity.

Other plus-sized games include Final Fantasy VII Remake Intergrade (90GB), Split Fiction (70GB), Cyberpunk 2077 (60GB), and Hyrule Warriors: Age of Imprisonment (44GB).

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time tops out at about 27GB. Nowadays it's completely possible to download just three or four games and find yourself completely out of onboard storage.

Should You Wait for Black Friday on November 27?

Black Friday deals are more confusing than ever these days. Most retailers spend November teasing limited-time offers, but the reality is that the deepest discounts rarely arrive until about a week before what I like to call "Black Friday proper."

Having tracked Nintendo sales for years, one thing is clear: once a Switch deal hits (like it is on November 22), it usually sticks for the rest of the sale. That means the prices you see now on consoles, games, and accessories are very likely the ones that’ll hold through to December. If you’ve been holding out for a solid deal, there’s no need to wait any longer.

These offers are reliable, worthwhile, and unlikely to get any better. Grab the games and hardware you’ve had your eye on, there’s no risk of Black Friday regret, only the satisfaction of finally getting exactly what you wanted at a price that makes sense.

Are you planning to pick up anything in Nintendo's Black Friday sale? Let us know in the comments, and stick around with IGN as we continue to update you daily on the best Black Friday deals for 2026.

Robert Anderson is a Senior Commerce Editor for IGN. Based in London, UK, he is a qualified journalist with a Bachelor of Arts in Journalism (First Class Degree) and over seven years of professional writing and editing experience.

You can usually find Robert lost in open-world RPG games like Elden Ring and Cyberpunk 2077. Outside of gaming, his passions include reading comics (especially Superman, Batman, and Spider-Man), taking photos, and keeping up with the latest in film and TV.

articles.title: Nintendo Switch 2 Gets First-Ever Official Black Friday Discount, Dropping Mario Kart World Bundle to $499
articles.summary: Nintendo's first official Switch 2 Black Friday deal is live for a limited time, bundling a flagship game and free bonus perks while undoing September's price hike.
articles.body:
Nintendo's Black Friday sale is now live , and it includes a $50 discount on a Switch 2 bundle deal . This is the first official discount the console has received since its launch in June 2025.

Originally priced at $549.99, including Mario Kart World and a three-month membership to Nintendo Switch Online, it is now down to $499.99 at all major US retailers until December 5.

Nintendo Switch 2 + Mario Kart World Bundle

The bundle would typically save buyers around $38. But now, with the Black Friday discount applied , savings are closer to $88 in total . $499.99 also matches the Switch 2's current MSRP, making this a standout Black Friday offer for gamers.

Earlier this year, Nintendo issued a price rise for the Switch 2 in the US and other international markets. The price rose from $449.99 to $499.99 in September 2026.

But, the new Black Friday deal effectively resets the price hike and offers gamers a real opportunity to save before the holidays, perfect for anyone looking for an amazing gift for a loved one, or even just for yourself!

Considering how expensive gaming is in 2026, especially when it comes to buying a console, this deal feels fairly significant in the grand scheme of the sale. As a reminder, neither the PS5 or Xbox Series consoles will be included in any official Black Friday sales this year.

Moreover, if you're waiting for any further Black Friday discounts on the Switch 2, you'll be waiting a long time. This is the only significant discount you're going to get over the next couple of weeks.

If you're picking the bundle up and are looking for a few extras to go alongside, Nintendo's sale also extends to a whole bunch of great Switch 2 games , alongside accessories like Samsung Memory Cards .

Highlights from this selection of deals include Resident Evil Requiem , Pragmata , and Elden Ring's Tarnished Edition . Some have even dropped to record-low prices there, so it's an excellent time to shop around.

First party options also include Donkey Kong Bananza and Kirby Air Riders, both down to $49.99, with $20 in savings, while even more third party games steal the spotlight, at least for me, with FF7 Remake and Rebirth down to $19.99 and $24.99 respectively.

Super Mario Party Jamboree + Jamboree TV

Super Mario Galaxy + Super Mario Galaxy 2

Amazon has also dropped the price of the highly rated Samsung P9 256GB Micro SDXC Express Card to $44.99 with free shipping. This is a slight $3 price drop from earlier this month and the lowest price I've seen in a while.

The 512GB model is also on sale for $99.99. Are these the lowest prices ever ? No. Are there cheaper memory cards out there? Yes . But if you're looking for a memory card that we've personally tested and recommend , you won't find a better deal right now.

Should You Wait for Black Friday on November 27?

Black Friday deals are more confusing than ever these days. Most retailers spend November teasing limited-time offers, but the reality is that the deepest discounts rarely arrive until about a week before what I like to call "Black Friday proper."

Having tracked Nintendo sales for years, one thing is clear: once a deal like this hits, it sticks for the rest of the sale. If you’ve been holding out for a solid deal, there’s no need to wait any longer, especially as often enough these top deals can sell out incredibly fast.

Are you planning to pick up anything in Nintendo's Black Friday sale? Let us know in the comments, and stick around with IGN as we continue to update you daily on the best Black Friday deals for 2026.

Robert Anderson is a Senior Commerce Editor for IGN. Based in London, UK, he is a qualified journalist with a Bachelor of Arts in Journalism (First Class Degree) and over seven years of professional writing and editing experience.

You can usually find Robert lost in open-world RPG games like Elden Ring and Cyberpunk 2077. Outside of gaming, his passions include reading comics (especially Superman, Batman, and Spider-Man), taking photos, and keeping up with the latest in film and TV.

articles.title: Nintendo Knocks $20 off Physical Switch 2 Copies of Donkey Kong Bananza for Black Friday
articles.summary: Physical copies of Donkey Kong Bananza have received a $20 discount in Nintendo's Black Friday sale, bringing its price down to $49.99.
articles.body:
Nintendo is officially joining PlayStation and Xbox in launching its own official Black Friday sale for this year. Alongside a very welcome Switch 2 console deal, the sale is also stacked with plenty of physical game deals for the OG Switch and Switch 2. One of our favorite finds for the latter console is Donkey Kong Bananza , which has received a $20 discount that's brought its price down to $49.99.

We've never seen the price for this game drop this low before, which certainly makes the deal a highlight among Nintendo's Black Friday sale selection.

If you've been saving a spot for it in your Switch 2 library, now is a great time to buy. We certainly think the game is worth it, as not only did it earn a 10/10 review score but it's also among our 100 best Nintendo Games of all time and was our favorite Nintendo game of last year .

Nintendo Switch 2 + Mario Kart World Bundle

Donkey Kong Bananza's review featured some mighty high praise from IGN's Logan Plant, who called it "a truly groundbreaking 3D platformer".

This is all thanks to "satisfying movement, powerful abilities, impressive destructible environments, and clever challenges," which ultimately earned it the title of "Masterpiece". It certainly sounds like a must-play if you've got a Switch 2, and what better time to grab it than when it's $20 off?

While Donkey Kong Bananza is easily one of our top deals out of Nintendo's Black Friday sale this year, it's not the only one available. Check out our full breakdown of the sale here to see what other game deals have caught our eye, alongside discounts on hardware and accessories.

As mentioned before, there's also a surprise Switch 2 console deal available at the moment, which is a joy to see after recent price hikes .

The sale runs until November 29 this year, so be quick to grab your favorite deals while they're still in stock.

Hannah Hoolihan is a freelancer who writes with the commerce team here at IGN.

articles.title: 10 Best Early Black Friday Gaming Deals You Can Already Shop
articles.summary: These are IGN's top 10 early Black Friday gaming deal recommendations you should actually consider buying before the big day on November 27.
articles.body:
Black Friday can be a bit of a nightmare to navigate. Trust me, I've been writing about it long enough to know how painfully annoying it can be for everywhere to have a sale, simply making things a bit more muddy when you're trying to find some genuinely good discounts.

That's especially true for gamers, and considering how expensive our favorite hobby is getting these days, I feel rather passionate about making sure everyone has the best opportunity possible to save as much as they can during the biggest sale event of the year.

GTA 6 might well be dominating mine and every other gamer's lives right now, but there's still plenty of other games to play, and I'm excited to highlight some tidy deals just below. Let's take a look at my top 10 Black Friday game deal picks that you can already shop today.

Nintendo Switch 2 + Mario Kart World Bundle

XBOX Wireless Controller – Forza Horizon 6 Limited Edition

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Switch 2 Digital)

Yeah, Black Friday is a bit weird. Most retailers tend to drag their sales out to no end in November, and then plenty even go that bit further and drag it into the December sales as well. That means, to no surprise, that Xbox , PlayStation , and Nintendo already have Black Friday sales live.

While the whole sale is still a strange semantic fever dream, this does benefit consumers in a couple of ways. First off, all the deals in the gaming sales are pretty much the exact same as you'll find on Nov. 27, just with less of an overwhelming sense of false urgency.

Even more so, some deals that go live before Black Friday proper tend to sell out, especially if the deal is actually decent. Therefore, doing a lot of your holiday shopping before Friday, in particular for gamers, tends to be the move. With that all being said, let's take a look at my first top pick in the Black Friday sale.

Let's kick things off with a big one. Nintendo's Black Friday sale is now live , and it includes a $50 discount on a Switch 2 bundle deal . This is the first official discount the console has received since its launch in June 2025.

Originally priced at $549.99, including Mario Kart World and a three-month membership to Nintendo Switch Online, it is now down to $499.99 at all major US retailers until December 5.

This is my hottest recommendation for the sale so far, especially as it's the only console deal we're getting this Black Friday. Snap it up while you still can, as I expect these to sell out fast over the next few days. I love my Switch 2, and this would make a great gift for any gamers in your life. You won't regret it.

50% off a PS5 exclusive only a year after it came out? Say less. This is an almighty good deal, and probably one of the best video game deals we'll see throughout the whole sale. It's so good, that most retailers are already low on stock. Amazon is sold out, so I'm recommending you check out either Walmart or go direct via PlayStation this time round.

Ghost of Yotei is a wonderful game that I finally got around to playing this year after missing out when it first launched in late 2025. There's been a recent DLC release for it as well, so there's whole lot of great content to dig through. Yes, I know plenty of us will be getting our open world fill with GTA 6 right now, but trust me, Ghost of Yotei is well worth your time as well, whether that's now or in the future. But, for now, this is the cheapest I expect we'll see it for a long time.

Not only that, this is physical copy exclusive deal - you can't find this discount on the PlayStation Store, so only those with a disc drive can take advantage. Yet another reason why it's important to preserve the physical media market. So, make your voice heard with this one, and buy a physical copy!

Back to something a little more premium, as Sony has graced us with a discount on the DualSense Edge Controller . It's $30 off at most retailers right now, for either the Black or the White variants.

I personally love the Black version of this controller, as those blue lights really do pop. Quick piece of advice from me, however, as these haven't got an excellent battery life. I'd recommend keeping it plugged in or charged when you're not using, similar to the standard DualSense controller. It's still a great controller, and much more worth it with its Black Friday discount, just not exactly rocking a premium battery life.

PlayStation DualSense Wireless Controller – Marathon Limited Edition

PlayStation DualSense Wireless Controller – Gray Camouflage

PlayStation DualSense Wireless Controller – Remix Green

PlayStation DualSense Wireless Controller – Rhythm Blue

PlayStation DualSense Wireless Controller – Techno Red

PlayStation DualSense Wireless Controller – Cosmic Red

PlayStation DualSense Wireless Controller - White

PlayStation DualSense Wireless Controller – Starlight Blue

PlayStation DualSense Wireless Controller – Galactic Purple

PlayStation DualSense Wireless Controller – Midnight Black

PlayStation DualSense Wireless Controller - Sterling Silver

PlayStation DualSense Wireless Controller – Chroma Teal

PlayStation DualSense Wireless Controller – Chroma Indigo

PlayStation DualSense Wireless Controller – Chroma Pearl

PlayStation DualSense Wireless Controller – 007 First Light Limited Edition

While we're on the subject, PS5 DualSense controllers are also discounted in the Black Friday sales right now. Most color variants are $20 off, so you can take your pick on which you'd like to buy.

I buy way too many controllers, so I will be restraining myself this year. But, if I had to suggest any of these, I'd recommend the funky Hyperpop collection for $64.88, the Gray Camo for $54, or the James Bond 007 First Light gamepad for $64.88.

Quick request from me, if you are buying another controller, and that tips you over into having more than four, maybe considering donating one to your sibling or a local charity.

Apparently this is the section where I talk about controllers. More games coming up next, but for now, the Forza Horizon 6 LE controller is down to just $49 at Walmart right now. For a limited edition gamepad, and probably one of the bets looking ones I've ever seen, this is a tremendous deal.

Considering standard Xbox controllers have only dropped as low as $43 in the sale so far , I think $6 more for a fancy looking controller like this one is a damn good deal. I'd take that deal.

Full disclosure, I have not play FF7 Rebirth on the Switch 2, nor any other console. I have been told it's a great game, and plays especially well on Nintendo's portable console.

But, what I do know, is that I've been covering FF7 Rebirth deals since its release. I've also covered it when it released for the Switch 2, and this is the best deal I've seen on the game so far for the console. The next best was $34.99 in the recent Amazon Prime Big Deal Days Sale , and this is even better.

While it doesn't reach the lows of $16.99 we saw for the PS5, it's still a fantastic deal and the lowest we've ever had on Switch 2, so you can't complain too much. FF7 Remake is also down to $19.99 , again it's lowest price on Switch 2, if you want to pick up both at the same time.

Game of the Year contender Resident Evil Requiem is also on sale for Black Friday, and down to $39.99. I love this game, and it inspired a big ol' Resident Evil replay marathon of mine this year.

This is the lowest price we've seen on the game so far this year, with a $30 discount for Switch 2, Xbox, and PS5, and $10 less than we saw during the recent Prime Day sale (its previous best price drop).

I played this on my Xbox Series X, and the game ran smooth as butter. I've not checked it out on Switch 2 yet, but I have heard it runs surprisingly well!

Whatever console you choose to play it on, I highly recommend checking out RE9 if you haven't played it yet. It's genuinely up there with RE4 for me. Please play it.

Another banger for 2026, Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced is a beautiful remake of one of my favorite games ever made.

I will admit, this didn't click with me as well as the original did back in the day, but it's still a wonderful game to mess around in, and the ship combat is unmatched for pure fun. Just sail around, blow up some ships, steal some treasure, and stick around for the surprisingly good story.

With a $15 discount, this is one of those deals where it's like, well it's not a massive discount, but its the best you're going to get for a while, and probably worth buying if you've been looking to play it soon.

Ubisoft isn't scared of a discount, however, so if you think you can stick it out for a bit longer to save that bit more, I can see this dropping to $35-$40 in one of the sales in 2027.

$5 off a masterpiece is still $5 off a masterpiece. What else do I have to say? Nintendo has created probably one of their best looking games ever, with perfect art direction, and just so happen to have done it with their best game ever. Say less, it's a small discount (and digital only ) but if you haven't played Ocarina of Time yet, you should be buying this immediately. If you haven't got a Switch 2, may I present a very good reason to get one!

Finishing things off with another nod to the Switch 2 Black Friday sale, and with very good reason after discussing a digital Switch 2 game deal.

Switch 2 consoles come packed with 256GB of storage. And, we all know that while that's an improvement over the OG Switch, it can still be a little tight when it comes to modern day gaming.

If you haven't yet, I'd suggest picking up a Switch 2 memory card in the sale, such as this Samsung P9 Express microSDXC. It's the cheapest you'll find an SD card that's compatible with the console in the sale right now, so well worth the recommendation.

But, I will say, this isn't the cheapest we've seen on these this year. That being said, with how bad things are in the tech industry again (i.e shortages making everything really expensive, thanks AI), I'd be thankful these aren't costing us a lot more.

Robert Anderson is a Senior Commerce Editor for IGN. Based in London, UK, he is a qualified journalist with a Bachelor of Arts in Journalism (First Class Degree) and over seven years of professional writing and editing experience.

You can usually find Robert lost in open-world RPG games like Elden Ring and Cyberpunk 2077. Outside of gaming, his passions include reading comics (especially Superman, Batman, and Spider-Man), taking photos, and keeping up with the latest in film and TV.

His primary coverage focuses on tracking down the best gaming deals and diving into the fast-paced world of Trading Card Games (TCGs). He regularly covers everything from the latest releases in Pokémon TCG and the most expensive cards to comprehensive Magic: The Gathering buying guides .
